claims.text: Random-solid-solution HfNbTaTiZr has high chemical disorder.
Atomic-size mismatch causes significant local lattice distortion in random-solid-solution HfNbTaTiZr.
Monte Carlo or hybrid MD/MC treatment can induce HfTi and TiZr short-range-order clusters and drive HfNbTaTiZr toward percolating B2-like structures.
Ordered B2-like HfTi/TiZr domains have lower RMS lattice distortion and atomic displacement amplitudes than the random solid solution.
Reduced local strain fields lower the scattering cross-section for high-frequency phonons.
Ordering changes HfNbTaTiZr from a mass-disorder-plus-strain-disorder regime to a mass-disorder-plus-reduced-strain-disorder regime.
Negative formation enthalpies of HfTi or TiZr pairs drive the proposed B2-like ordering.
B2-like ordering creates a more regular local environment and reduces the variance of atomic force constants and atomic displacements.
The reduction in strain-related scattering outweighs scattering introduced by chemical ordering.
Percolation of low-distortion HfTi/TiZr regions creates continuous high-conductivity pathways for high-frequency phonons.
The proposed ordering and percolation increase the mean free path of high-frequency phonons.
The ordered state will have 10–25% higher lattice thermal conductivity than the random solid solution between 300 K and 800 K.
High-frequency phonon-DOS peaks will narrow upon ordering relative to their disorder-broadened form in the random solid solution.
The group velocity of high-frequency phonon modes will increase upon ordering.
Debye-Waller factors will be lower in ordered regions than in the random solid solution.
A conductivity increase requires the short-range order to form a percolating network of ordered B2-like structures.
If short-range order remains as isolated clusters or becomes amorphous-like, lattice thermal conductivity will decrease.
Ordering that produces substantial mass contrast without reducing strain will decrease lattice thermal conductivity.
The conductivity enhancement is most pronounced from 300 K to 800 K because phonon-phonon scattering is not yet dominant.
